A data driven analysis of package volume in the face of developers’ claims of wild productivity with AI tools. The authors claims most of the software being produced quickly is software for working with AI but that the industry as a whole isn’t moving meaningfully faster. Personally, I use AI to build an order of magnitude more software than I used to but I don’t release it. I build personal tools with a small audience (maybe even just me) and push them to private GitHub repos. So this analysis doesn’t surprise me too much. AI is enabling the creation of a different type of software. Package creation was more popular when software was expensive. Now that it’s cheap the primitive are different.
